qt: to the Commission Ľuboš Blaha (NI) Subject:

The infamous Ukrainian website Myrotvorets, known to be linked to several Ukrainian politicians, publishes an unofficial kill list of enemies of the Ukrainian regime. Some people have even been murdered after their details were shared on the site – for example, the journalist and writer Oles Buzyna and the former Ukrainian MP Oleh Kalashnikov. Several Members of the European Parliament are also named on the Myrotvorets kill list, including Ľuboš Blaha, Ewa Zajączkowska-Hernik, Christophe Gomart, Danilo Della Valle, Eero Heinäluoma, Petar Volgin, Fidias Panayiotou and Elena Kountoura. The list also apparently includes other serving and former MEPs. 1.
Is the Commission planning to take any action to protect EU representatives in response to this threat?

The Commission has discussed the issue of the Myrotvorets database before, in 2022 and 2024. In response to a parliamentary question about Myrotvorets1, the VicePresident of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Josep Borrell stated that the EU had already raised the issue with Ukrainian officials and would continue to follow up on it. Did those discussions ever get beyond the topic of protection of personal data in accordance with European standards?

Recently, one more name was added to the Myrotvorets kill list: that of a 14-year-old boy who had been tortured at a facility in Petropavlivska Borshchahivka, allegedly for agitating against mobilisation and attacking army personnel. Will the Commission condemn this outrageous violation of European values?
